newsitem.title: USA: Delhi starts South Texas expansion.
newsitem.headline: Delhi starts South Texas expansion.

text.p: Delhi Gas Pipeline Corp has started a major expansion program in South Texas scheduled to be operational by November 1, USX-Delhi Group said Wednesday.

The expansion will include interconnecting Delhi's existing South Texas assets with 53 miles of 16- and 20-inch natural gas pipeline, adding treating facilities and increasing the processing capacity of its Three Rivers Processing Plant in Live Oak County to 120 million cubic feet of natural gas per day from 30 million.

To connect its existing South Texas gathering systems, Delhi said, it will install a 13-mile, 20-inch pipeline originating at its existing Three Rivers plant and extending into an active drilling area of southern Live Oak County, which includes the Tom Lyne Field. The remaining 40 miles of 16-inch pipe will connect the new 20-inch line to Delhi's existing 390-mile Laredo Lopeno System in Webb County. On the Live Oak end of the new pipeline, Delhi has a combined 475 miles of pipeline including the Live Oak and Blessing Victoria systems which are already interconnected.
Additional gas processing capacity at the Three Rivers plant will result from a plant acquisition and relocation.

Delhi said it has acquired the 90 million cubic feet per day capacity Hooker Processing Plant in Texas County, Oklahoma from Timberland Gathering & Processing Company Inc, a subsidiary of Cross Timbers Oil Co, for undisclosed terms. This plant will be located on a site adjacent to the existing Three Rivers plant between San Antonio and Corpus Christi.

The relocated cryogenic processing plant will be retrofitted to an Ortloff Gas Subcooled process design to achieve high natural gas liquid recoveries, maximize capacity and achieve state-of-the-art efficiencies. Additionally, a new 250 gallons per minute front end amine treating facility has been acquired to accommodate new gas supplies having increasing levels of carbon dioxide.

In conjunction with its expansion plans, Delhi has entered into a new long-term gathering, treating and processing agreement with Vastar Resources Inc, for its production in the Tom Lyne and Clay West Fields in southern Live Oak County and the West Rhode Ranch Field in McMullen County.

USX-Delhi Group, a Dallas-based unit of USX Corp, includes Delhi Gas Pipeline Corp and certain other subsidiaries of USX. They are engaged in the purchasing, gathering, processing, treating, transporting and marketing of natural gas.
